articles.headline: US warns West Asian allies to prepare for possible Iran military strikes
articles.title: U.S. warns allies to prepare for possible Iran strikes, retaliation after elections, say sources
articles.summary: United States officials have advised several West Asian governments to prepare for potential military action against Iran following the United States midterm elections on November 3, 2026. According to two anonymous diplomats, the campaign could last several days and trigger regional retaliation targeting infrastructure. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi stated that Tehran continues pursuing diplomatic solutions, while the United Arab Emirates urged political restraint to prevent wider conflict.
articles.description: The U.S. has told regional allies that the new round of military action could last for several days, but regional officials are bracing for Iran and its proxy groups to retaliate — leading to a fight that could last even longer, the sources said

articles.headline: Israel election results show no clear winner as vote counting continues
articles.title: No clear winner in Israel election with nearly 90 percent of votes counted
articles.summary: Nearly ninety percent of ballots have been counted in Israel, leaving both major political blocs short of the sixty-one seats needed to form a government. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s bloc leads with fifty-three projected seats, while Gadi Eisenkot’s opposition bloc expects forty-eight. Final results are expected as soon as Thursday evening. President Isaac Herzog will begin consultations with party leaders next week.
articles.description: Netanyahu's right-wing bloc leads but is falling short of the votes needed to form a government.

articles.headline: High-speed train crash kills dozens of people in central Spain
articles.title: High-speed train crash kills at least 68 people in Spain
articles.summary: A devastating collision between two high-speed trains occurred on Wednesday morning approximately 140km south of Madrid, resulting in at least 68 fatalities and numerous injuries. Spain's Transport Minister Óscar Puente attributed the disaster to a computer failure followed by an erroneous instruction from a control centre to resume movement without speed restrictions. Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez announced that the government is investigating potential security system failures.
articles.description: The crash, between a moving train and another that was stopped further up the track, was caused by an "inexplicable" error, the transport minister said.

articles.headline: Spain demands answers after deadliest train disaster in over a decade
articles.title: Spain demands answers after deadliest train disaster in over a decade
articles.description: At least 68 people have been killed and more than 100 injured after two high-speed trains collided south of Madrid.

articles.headline: US Federal Reserve maintains interest rates steady amid surging inflation
articles.title: Fed leaves interest rates unchanged despite inflation in the US
articles.summary: The United States Federal Reserve held benchmark interest rates steady at 3.75 to 4 percent following a 10-2 vote announced on Wednesday, maintaining monetary policy despite annual inflation rising to 3.7 percent in September. The decision precedes upcoming economic data releases and follows a rate hike last month, while the central bank's next meeting is scheduled for December.
articles.description: Rates will remain 3.75-4 percent even as inflation continues to rise.

articles.headline: US Federal Reserve holds interest rates steady amid surging inflation
articles.title: U.S. Fed holds interest rates steady despite surging inflation
articles.summary: The Federal Open Market Committee voted 10-2 to maintain interest rates between 3.75 and 4.00 percent on Wednesday, October 28, 2026, citing the need for more economic data. The decision comes ahead of midterm elections and follows US President Donald Trump's energy and tariff policies, which have driven inflation while the unemployment rate remains near 4.2 percent.
articles.description: The 12-member FOMC voted 10-2 to hold rates at a target range between 3.75 and 4.00%, citing the need for more data in the fight against inflation

articles.headline: Deadly high-speed train collision in Spain
articles.title: Deadly high-speed train collision in Spain
articles.description: At least 39 people have been killed after two high-speed trains collided near Urda, Spain.

articles.headline: Finland and Norway leaders discuss Ukraine peace efforts in rare call with Putin
articles.title: Norway and Finland leaders hold rare call with Putin
articles.summary: The leaders of Finland and Norway held a ninety-minute call with Russian President Vladimir Putin to discuss diplomatic efforts regarding the war in Ukraine. Finnish President Alexander Stubb and Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Stre stated the initiative aimed to convey direct messages on future peace negotiations. The Kremlin reported Putin emphasized that a lasting peace requires considering Russia's interests.
articles.description: An end to the conflict in Ukraine "will not be achieved through silence," Finland's President Alexander Stubb said.

articles.headline: Russia intercepts majority of over six hundred drones launched toward Moscow
articles.title: Russia says more than 600 drones launched towards Moscow overnight
articles.summary: Russian air defence forces intercepted most of the 613 drones launched toward Moscow overnight, according to state news agency TASS. Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin reported on Telegram that 231 unmanned aerial vehicles were destroyed on approach, while the rest were neutralised on distant paths between Wednesday and Thursday. Meanwhile, a separate strike damaged an educational institution in Kharkiv.
articles.description: The attack is the latest in a series of major drone assaults targeting the Moscow region.

articles.headline: Pentagon military planner fired as United States considers potential Iran strikes
articles.title: Hegseth fires Pentagon's top military planner even as Trump considers new Iran strikes
articles.summary: Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth removed Army Lieutenant General Brett Sylvia as head of strategy, plans and policy on the Joint Chiefs of Staff. A defence official confirmed the dismissal on Wednesday as President Donald Trump considers new military operations against Iran following an eight-month-long war. Sylvia is the second general to be ousted from the J5 post during Hegseth's tenure.
articles.description: The defence official, who spoke on condition of anonymity to discuss sensitive personnel matters, said there is no immediate replacement for Mr. Sylvia and no reason has been given for the firing

articles.headline: Federal judge rejects challenge to California noncitizen voter ballots
articles.title: Judge rejects Trump effort to block California ‘noncitizen’ ballots
articles.summary: United States District Judge David Carter on Wednesday rejected a Department of Justice request to temporarily stop California from counting mail ballots from 20,000 alleged noncitizens. The ruling came six days before the midterm elections as the Trump administration expands voter investigations across at least 13 states. The Justice Department swiftly appealed the decision to the Ninth US Circuit Court of Appeals.
articles.description: More than 100 subpoenas issued across 13 states as government ramps up search for alleged noncitizen voters.

articles.headline: Train collision in Spain leaves at least 30 people dead
articles.title: What we know so far about deadly Spain train crash
articles.summary: At least 30 people died when two trains collided south of Madrid on Wednesday morning, according to local media citing the regional government. State-owned Renfe and private operator Iryo trains crashed between Mora and Orgaz at around 09:00 local time, carrying over 500 passengers combined. Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez and the royal family expressed shock while emergency services deployed helicopters and fire crews to the scene.
articles.description: More than 500 passengers were on board the trains when the crash occurred in the province of Toledo, south of Madrid.

articles.headline: Activists accuse Israeli settlers of assaulting foreign nationals in West Bank
articles.title: Activists accuse Israeli settlers of assault in occupied West Bank
articles.summary: Russian activist Adele Shoko reported that armed Israeli settlers attacked her and two colleagues in the Palestinian village of Umm al-Khair within the occupied West Bank. According to Shoko, the victims suffered physical abuse and detention by authorities following the incident. This event follows an earlier October 16 attack in Abu Falah where masked settlers targeted Palestinian olive farmers and injured Washington Post photojournalist Heidi Levine.
articles.description: Footage shows men, some armed, beating a US journalist and an Israeli-Russian activist in Umm al-Khair.

articles.headline: Drone strikes on Darfur market in Sudan kill over one hundred people
articles.title: Strikes on Darfur market in Sudan killed more than 100, rights group says
articles.summary: Military drone strikes targeting a busy market in Nyala, South Darfur, killed more than 100 people, predominantly women and children, according to the rights group Emergency Lawyers. Witnesses reported that the attack struck an area frequented by paramilitary Rapid Support Forces fighters and civilian vendors. Doctors Without Borders stated that a local hospital received 36 bodies and treated over 150 wounded individuals following the bombardment.
articles.description: Women and children killed as witnesses say attack struck civilian shopkeepers, RSF fighters.

articles.headline: Israeli settlers savagely attack journalists in occupied West Bank
articles.title: Israeli settlers savagely attack journalists in occupied West Bank
articles.description: Videos circulating on social media show Israeli settlers assaulting three foreign journalists in the West Bank

articles.headline: Serbians storm TV studio as pro-Vucic media faces reckoning
articles.title: Serbians storm TV studio as pro-Vucic media faces reckoning
articles.description: Serbians stormed a TV studio and confronted its editor-in-chief after a student-led protest movement swept into power.

articles.headline: Poland pivots toward India to strengthen economic and defense cooperation
articles.title: Poland pivots towards India as ‘strategic partnership’ with China develops cracks
articles.summary: Poland is strengthening its strategic partnership with India through improved economic and defense collaboration following Prime Minister Donald Tusk’s recent visit. This diplomatic shift comes as Warsaw distances itself from China due to trade imbalances and concerns regarding the Russia-Ukraine war. A recent Polish government study warned that European industries face significant economic pressure and job losses from Chinese state-led industrial strategies.
articles.description: Poland and India seek to raise bilateral trade from $6 bn to $10 bn; PM Modi visited Poland in 2024, during which ties were elevated to ‘strategic partnership’; Warsaw is also trying to diversify partnerships as trade imbalance and Beijing’s support for Russia deepen disillusionment with China

articles.headline: Cabinet approves three percent dearness allowance hike for central employees
articles.title: Cabinet approves 3% hike in dearness allowance for central government employees
articles.summary: The Union Cabinet approved a three percent increase in dearness allowance and dearness relief on October 28, 2026, benefiting over 1.17 crore central government employees and pensioners ahead of Diwali. Information and Broadcasting Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw stated the hike is effective from July 1, 2026. Additionally, the Cabinet cleared the Container Manufacturing Promotion Scheme with a budgetary outlay of Rs 10,000 crore.
articles.description: The DA and DR increase will be effective from July 1, 2026 and will benefit 48.54 lakh employees and 68.71 lakh pensioners

articles.headline: Flávio Bolsonaro arrives in Miami after losing Brazilian presidential election
articles.title: Flávio Bolsonaro denies fleeing Brazil after landing in Miami
articles.summary: Brazilian Senator Flávio Bolsonaro arrived in Miami after traveling through Argentina following his defeat in Sunday's presidential run-off election against Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva. The United States State Department granted visas to Bolsonaro and his family, while Brazilian authorities have cancelled his passport and continue investigations into alleged money laundering and banking irregularities.
articles.description: The defeated Brazilian candidate claims to be the victim of a coup d’état and political persecution, recycling unsubstantiated allegations of “electoral fraud”.

articles.headline: Riot police deployed in Madrid as protests erupt over deadly train crash
articles.title: Riot police deployed in Madrid as protests erupt over deadly train crash
articles.description: A deadly train crash fuelled anger in Spain as far-right demonstrators clashed with police

articles.headline: Himalayan building boom puts hundreds of thousands at disaster risk
articles.title: Building boom puts 300,000 people in the path of potential Himalayan disasters
articles.summary: A peer-reviewed study published in Scientific Reports indicates that at least 300,000 individuals in the Himalayan region now reside in high-risk hazard zones. Researchers discovered that built-up land across northern Nepal, south-eastern Tibet, and India's Uttarakhand expanded by approximately 45 percent between 2016 and 2023. Scientists attribute the escalating threat of floods and landslides primarily to rapid regional temperature warming that accelerates glacial melting.
articles.description: The construction of tourism facilities, housing, and infrastructure has surged in parts of Nepal and India's Uttarakhand.

articles.headline: Survivors recount horror following deadly high-speed train collision in Spain
articles.title: Bloodied, dazed and angry - how passengers' rail journey turned to disaster in Spain
articles.summary: Passengers aboard two southward-bound trains traveling from Madrid to Seville experienced severe trauma when a state-operated Renfe train collided with a stationary Iryo private train on Wednesday. Survivors described being thrown into the air, falling among debris, and witnessing fatalities and severe injuries. Spain's Transport Minister Óscar Puente stated that the Renfe train was erroneously ordered to proceed following an automatic signalling system failure.
articles.description: Survivors of the train crash in Spain have spoken of their shock, panic and anger at the accident in Toledo province on Wednesday.

articles.headline: Israel faces political deadlock and deep societal divisions following election
articles.title: Israel's election deadlock is a sign of the country's deep divisions
articles.summary: Israel faces an inconclusive election result leaving neither political bloc with a parliamentary majority after record voter turnout. President Isaac Herzog warned against government instability amid deep societal tensions between religious and secular populations, ultra-Orthodox military exemptions, and opposing views on leadership under Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
articles.description: The election was a celebration of democracy in some ways - but it has left Israel with no clear path to a new government, writes James Landale.

articles.headline: Netanyahu leads Israel election with partial results showing no majority
articles.title: Netanyahu's bloc leading Israel election but short of majority, partial results show
articles.summary: Partial results from Israel's general election on October 27, 2026, indicate Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's right-wing bloc leads rival Gadi Eisenkot, though both remain short of a parliamentary majority. With high voter turnout recorded across the country, Arab-led parties are positioned to win a record number of seats, potentially serving as crucial kingmakers as President Isaac Herzog prepares to oversee coalition negotiations.
articles.description: With 85% of ballots counted, Netanyahu's Likud party and its allies are set to win 53 seats in the 120-seat Knesset.

articles.headline: United Nations General Assembly votes to condemn United States embargo of Cuba
articles.title: UN votes to condemn embargo of Cuba despite US lobbying push
articles.summary: The United Nations General Assembly voted 130 to 17 on Wednesday to condemn the United States economic embargo against Cuba, despite American diplomatic pressure that increased abstentions. Cuban Foreign Minister Bruno Rodriguez criticized the decades-long restrictions, while US Ambassador to the United Nations Mike Waltz announced the expulsion of a Cuban diplomat following an altercation.
articles.description: US points to increase in abstentions in General Assembly as evidence that push to isolate Cuba is slowly succeeding.

articles.headline: U.S. labour leader and civil rights icon Dolores Huerta dies at 96
articles.title: Pioneering U.S. labour leader Dolores Huerta dies at 96
articles.summary: Dolores Huerta, a prominent United States labour leader and civil rights icon who co-founded the United Farm Workers union, passed away on October 28, 2026, at the age of 96, according to her family. Throughout her career, she organised strikes to improve conditions for migrant workers and received accolades such as the presidential medal of freedom from Barack Obama.
articles.description: Dolores Huerta took the reins of the U.S. farmworker movement in the 1960s with Chavez

articles.headline: Google releases new Gemini 4 Carbon model with advanced cybersecurity features
articles.title: Google launches Gemini 4 Carbon with a ‘significant leap’ in cybersecurity
articles.summary: Google has announced the release of Gemini 4 Carbon, its latest frontier model featuring significant improvements in coding and cybersecurity. Available initially to select defense companies through the Fairwind Program at an introductory price of $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens, the model excels at discovering real-world bugs and generating secure code.
articles.description: Google has released its latest frontier model, Gemini 4 Carbon, offering "significant gains" in coding, agentic tasks, and cybersecurity. In an announcement on Wednesday, Google highlights Carbon's top spot on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index (v5.0) benchmark, with Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra trailing behind. The new Gemini 4 Carbon model offers improvements over […]

articles.headline: Cyclone Arnab impacts 17 Odisha districts as heavy rainfall triggers flood warnings
articles.title: Cyclone Arnab: 17 Odisha districts affected by heavy rain, Gajapati worst hit
articles.summary: Seventeen districts in Odisha have been affected by heavy rainfall brought by severe cyclonic storm Arnab, which crossed the Andhra Pradesh coast on October 28, 2026. Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi stated that authorities evacuated 43,827 people to 634 relief camps, while the Central Water Commission warned of potential flooding across multiple river basins due to ongoing extreme weather.
articles.description: As many as 2,245 pregnant women were shifted to nearby health centres, while 931 babies were born during the disaster

articles.headline: High Arab voter turnout surges in Israeli legislative elections
articles.title: What has driven the high Arab turnout in Israel’s elections?
articles.summary: Israel recorded a 77.7% voter turnout in the October 27, 2026, legislative elections, driven significantly by a surge among Arab citizens. Exit polls estimated Arab participation at nearly 80%, largely motivated by fear of a right-wing government under Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. This high participation positions Arab parties to potentially secure at least 17 Knesset seats and influence coalition formation.
articles.description: Arab voter turnout is estimated to be nearly 80%, the highest in at least a decade, according to exit polls

articles.headline: Putin: Russia is African continent’s best partner, not ‘colonial’ West
articles.title: Putin: Russia is African continent’s best partner, not ‘colonial’ West
articles.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin told the leaders of dozens of African nations that Moscow was their best partner.

articles.headline: Israel faces political deadlock after general election yields no clear winner
articles.title: What are the implications of Israel’s elections?
articles.summary: Israel's first election since the October 7 attacks concluded with a record turnout but failed to produce a clear winner, leaving Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's right-wing alliance short of a majority. The main opposition bloc led by Gadi Eisenkot also lacks the numbers to govern alone, while Arab-led lists achieved unprecedented electoral gains during the closely watched contest.
articles.description: No clear winner in Israel's first election since the October 7 attacks and genocidal war in Gaza.

articles.headline: Russian President Vladimir Putin denies neo-colonial exploitation at Russia-Africa Summit
articles.title: Putin tells African leaders Moscow will not pursue ‘neo-colonialism’
articles.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin addressed delegates from 48 African countries at the third Russia-Africa Summit in Moscow on October 28, 2026, stating that Moscow avoids neo-colonial exploitation. Putin criticised Western nations for predatory financial practices and highlighted that Russia supplied 13 million metric tonnes of agricultural products to Africa in the first nine months of the year.
articles.description: Speaking at the third Russia-Africa Summit, Putin frames Moscow as an alternative to former colonial powers.

articles.headline: UK Chancellor John Healey unveils Autumn Budget with new household support
articles.title: Five key takeaways from the UK Autumn Budget
articles.summary: Chancellor of the Exchequer John Healey unveiled the United Kingdom government budget on Wednesday, offering twenty million households a one-off payment of one hundred pounds towards energy bills. The package includes increased defence spending, higher minimum wages, and temporary bank corporation tax surcharges. According to the Office for Budget Responsibility, real earnings will see no growth next year.
articles.description: The United Kingdom's government says its policies are for the 'working people of Britain'.

articles.headline: Jerusalem Daily: What’s next after Israel’s elections?
articles.title: Jerusalem Daily: What’s next after Israel’s elections?
articles.description: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and former military chief Gadi Eisenkot are both claiming victory in Israel’s election

articles.headline: Neoliberal policies drive youth protests and economic frustration across G7 nations
articles.title: How neoliberalism turned the world against its young
articles.summary: Young people are leading widespread demonstrations in countries like France, Spain, and Albania amid severe economic challenges such as high unemployment, inflation, and declining real wages. Experts argue that aggressive neoliberal reductions in public welfare spending and capitalist decisions to limit labor demand have caused youth unemployment rates to soar to nearly double the overall averages.
articles.description: The rise in youth unrest stems from failures of neoliberal capitalism, which has weakened public welfare and worsened unemployment; as falling wages undermine consumption and investment, young people face fewer jobs, rising education costs and an economic system that prioritises profits

articles.headline: Iran warns of devastating economic fallout from any new Israeli attack
articles.title: Iran warns of 'devastating' economic fallout from any new Israeli attack
articles.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi warned on October 28, 2026, that any renewed Israeli military action would trigger severe international market disruptions, particularly affecting gas suppliers and consumers. Amid ongoing regional conflicts and blockades affecting energy shipments, Washington reportedly advised Gulf Arab nations to prepare for a potential military campaign following the November 3 U.S. midterm elections.
articles.description: Under Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who has vowed to topple Iran's government, the two countries have directly fought a war for the first time in their history after decades of enmity

articles.headline: Benjamin Netanyahu leads in Israel election after partial vote count
articles.title: Netanyahu bloc leads Israel vote, falls short of majority
articles.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu held a narrow lead with 55 of 120 parliament seats after fifty percent of votes were counted on October 28, 2026. His rival Gadi Eisenkot secured forty-nine seats, while Arab parties claimed sixteen. Neither bloc reached a majority, prompting expectations of extended coalition negotiations or potential new elections following the general vote.
articles.description: With more than three quarters of the vote counted, Mr. Netanyahu’s right-wing bloc was slightly ahead but short of a majority

articles.headline: Trump announces upcoming meeting between Putin and Zelensky
articles.title: Trump says Putin-Zelensky meeting to be set up 'very soon'
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump stated on October 28, 2026, that a face-to-face meeting between Russian President Vladimir Putin and Ukrainian counterpart Volodymyr Zelensky would be arranged very soon. The diplomatic push coincides with ongoing international efforts to end the multi-year conflict, though previous U.S.-led talks have stalled amid conflicting territorial objectives and persistent military casualties.
articles.description: "There'll be a meeting set up very soon and I think a lot of progress could be made," Mr. Trump told reporters

articles.headline: Ten people die in collision involving two high-speed trains in Toledo province
articles.title: At least 68 dead after two trains collide in Spain’s Toledo Province
articles.summary: At least ten people died following a collision between two trains in central Spain on October 28, 2026. According to rail operator ADIF, the crash occurred in Toledo province, disrupting services between Madrid, Ciudad Real, and Andalusia. State broadcaster TVE reported that one high-speed train struck the rear of another traveling in the same direction, causing carriages to derail.
articles.description: The second such accident to strike Spain this year will raise fresh questions about the country’s rail safety, with the Transport Minister speaking of an “error” and “inexplicable circumstances” that led to the collision.

articles.headline: Watch: At the scene of Spain's deadly train crash
articles.title: Watch: At the scene of Spain's deadly train crash
articles.description: People have been killed after a Spanish high-speed train collided with another train south of the capital Madrid, making this the country's worst disaster since 2013.

articles.headline: Bank of Canada raises key interest rate for first time in three years
articles.title: Bank of Canada raises interest rates for the first time in three years
articles.summary: The Bank of Canada increased its benchmark interest rate by a quarter point to 2.5 percent on October 28, 2026, marking the first hike in over three years. Governor Tiff Macklem cited rising energy costs and an upgraded inflation forecast of 3.1 percent for 2027 as primary drivers, while warning that additional rate increases might become necessary to control broader economic pressures.
articles.description: The central bank increased the key rate by a quarter point as soaring energy prices pushed up inflation.

articles.headline: Ethiopia acquires twelve Russian fighter jets and plans air defense purchase
articles.title: Ethiopia receives 12 Russian Su-35 jets, plans S-400 acquisition
articles.summary: Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed announced the delivery of twelve Su-35 fighter jets from Moscow during the Russia-Africa Summit on Wednesday. The aircraft arrived ahead of schedule to help Ethiopian armed forces defend airspace and deter aggression amid ongoing domestic conflicts in Tigray and Amhara regions. The prime minister also stated that the country will purchase four S-400 batteries.
articles.description: PM Abiy Ahmed makes announcement during a Moscow summit as Ethiopia battles armed groups in Tigray and Amhara.

articles.headline: Cyclone Arnab kills five people and batters north Andhra Pradesh with heavy rain
articles.title: 5 dead as Cyclone Arnab batters north Andhra with heavy rain
articles.summary: Severe Cyclonic Storm Arnab caused five fatalities and widespread damage across north Andhra Pradesh on October 27 and 28, 2026, according to official reports. Packing winds up to 150 kmph, the storm uprooted over 1,000 trees and flooded agricultural land across 80,500 hectares. Chief Minister N. Chandravabu Naidu announced relief packages including rice and essential food items for affected families.
articles.description: Extremely heavy rain and winds gusting up to 150 kmph lash coastal districts; over 1,000 trees uprooted, crops across 80,500 hectares affected

articles.headline: India faces structural challenges and middle-income trap amid weak job creation
articles.title: The way out of the dangerous trap
articles.summary: India is drifting toward a middle-income trap characterized by weak job creation, stagnant wages, sluggish private investment, and low productivity, threatening its rise to high-income status. Structural issues stem from institutions shaped by social norms that undervalue vocational education and manual skills. Chief Economic Adviser V Anantha Nageswaran recently urged youth to pursue trades instead of chasing software roles.
articles.description: India risks a middle-income, low-productivity trap as weak job creation, stagnant wages and sluggish investment reinforce one another; escaping it requires better vocational education, wider diffusion of technology and useful knowledge, and greater social value for skilled work

articles.headline: Government notifies personal details required for the 2027 Census population enumeration
articles.title: The concerns over the Census questions
articles.summary: The Central government notified the individual questions for the population enumeration phase of the 2027 Census last month. In a significant departure from previous surveys, respondents must provide parents and spouse details, declared nationality, permanent residential address, COVID-19 vaccination place, bank accounts, mobile numbers, Aadhaar, Voter ID, passport, and driving license availability.
articles.description: The questionnaire for the population enumeration phase of the 2027 Census comprises 40 questions and seek details such as nationality, number of bank accounts and mobile, Aadhaar and voter ID numbers, if available, raising concerns over its potential digression from the purpose of collecting data for policy and planning

articles.headline: Kremlin excludes European countries from upcoming talks with Ukraine and the United States
articles.title: Kremlin says European countries not included in next Ukraine talks
articles.summary: European nations will not participate in the upcoming discussions between Ukraine and the United States in Abu Dhabi, according to Kremlin foreign policy aide Yuri Ushakov. While Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy stated that Kyiv wants European involvement, differing accounts emerged regarding the trilateral meetings. Meanwhile, the Netherlands and Britain announced substantial new military and financial support packages for Ukraine.
articles.description: The comment comes as UK and Netherlands pledge extra military support for Kyiv.

articles.headline: Jio Platforms debuts strongly on stock exchanges amid broader market decline
articles.title: Jio Platforms debuts at 21% premium as Sensex slides; valuation tops ₹12 lakh crore
articles.summary: Jio Platforms Limited made a strong stock market debut on October 28, 2026, listing at 1,358 rupees for a 21.36 percent premium. Managing Director Akash Ambani noted the IPO was subscribed over 22 times. The market capitalization reached approximately 12.5 lakh crore rupees, making it India's second-most-valued listed company behind parent Reliance Industries.
articles.description: With a market capitalisation of around ₹12.5 lakh crore, JPL overtook Bharti Airtel to become India’s second-most-valued listed company after parent Reliance Industries.

articles.headline: Analysis highlights significant gap in official manufacturing sector GVA estimates
articles.title: The gap in manufacturing sector GVA
articles.summary: The National Statistical Office reported manufacturing gross value added at 38.6 lakh crore rupees for 2023-24 at current prices. An alternative estimate using official Annual Survey of Industries and Annual Survey of Unincorporated Sector Enterprises data sets the figure at 27.4 lakh crore rupees. This leaves an unexplained gap of 24.5 percent even after accounting for residual workers.
articles.description: According to the National Accounts Statistics, the manufacturing sector’s GVA is ₹38.6 lakh crore in 2023-24 at current prices.; however, an ‘Alternative Estimate’ using data from the Annual Survey of Industries and Annual Survey of Unincorporated Sector Enterprises gives a lower figure, prompting a closer look at the official estimate

articles.headline: Health experts criticize excessive cancer drug pricing following revised price lists
articles.title: Sharp cuts in price of cancer drugs expose excessive pricing, say health experts
articles.summary: Medical health activists stated on October 28, 2026, that revised Maximum Retail Price lists for anti-cancer medicines published by the National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority expose excessive pricing. The National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority released 543 brand prices effective November 9 following Trade Margin Rationalization. Activists argued that trade margin caps alone are insufficient to ensure affordability.
articles.description: NPPA releases revised MRPs for 543 brands of anti-cancer medicines with the new prices effective from November 9; Jan Swasthya Abhiyan India (JSA India) says controlling trade margins alone is insufficient as life-saving cancer treatment must be affordable based on medical need, not a patient’s ability to pay

articles.headline: Bolsonaro turns up in Florida after vanishing from public view
articles.title: Bolsonaro turns up in Florida after vanishing from public view
articles.description: Flavio Bolsonaro, Brazil’s defeated presidential candidate, landed in Florida after fleeing the country with his family.

articles.headline: Israeli president hopes to avoid new vote after inconclusive election results
articles.title: Israel president urges against new vote despite inconclusive result
articles.summary: President Isaac Herzog expressed hope on October 28, 2026, for avoiding a second election after an inconclusive vote on October 27 left Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot short of a majority. Netanyahu's bloc is projected to win 53 seats and Eisenkot's opposition 48 in the 120-seat parliament, with Arab lists projected to reach 19 seats.
articles.description: With more than 85% of ballots counted, Benjamin Netanyahu's right-wing bloc was slightly ahead but still short of a majority in the election

articles.headline: Flavio Bolsonaro arrives in Miami following his presidential election defeat in Brazil
articles.title: Flavio Bolsonaro lands in Miami after losing Brazil’s presidential election
articles.summary: Brazilian Senator Flavio Bolsonaro and his family arrived in Miami, Florida, on Wednesday morning after he lost the presidential election to incumbent Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva. Brazil's Supreme Court had ordered him to surrender his passports to prevent him from fleeing potential embezzlement and money laundering investigations before his senatorial immunity ended in January.
articles.description: Bolsonaro and his family have fled to the US amid a Brazilian Supreme Court order to surrender his passports.

articles.headline: Israel faces political deadlock as election results leave both leading blocs without majorities
articles.title: How could Israel break election deadlock? Here are four scenarios
articles.summary: Following Tuesday's election in Israel, neither Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's coalition nor challenger Gadi Eisenkot's bloc secured a parliamentary majority with 85% of votes counted. Potential resolutions include a national unity government, an opposition coalition reliant on Arab parties, right-wing defections to Netanyahu, or holding new elections, a recurring outcome between 2019 and 2022.
articles.description: With 85% of votes counted, all signs point to an impasse. The most likely outcome may be new elections.

articles.headline: Israel's election result is messy - here's why
articles.title: Israel's election result is messy - here's why
articles.description: Despite having the highest voter turnout in nearly three decades, Israel's elections have had no clear winner. What does this mean for the country, asks the BBC's Yolande Knell.

articles.headline: Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi meets Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa in Damascus
articles.title: Iraqi PM Ali al-Zaidi meets Ahmed al-Sharaa in historic Syria visit
articles.summary: Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi traveled to Damascus to meet Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa in the first such visit since Bashar al-Assad fell. According to the Iraqi News Agency, the leaders discussed expanding economic, oil, and agricultural cooperation, including exporting Iraqi oil through the Baniyas line following the outbreak of the United States-led war on Iran.
articles.description: Talks focused on enhancing trade, reviving Baniyas oil pipeline and achieving stability through cooperation.

articles.headline: Israeli election results show no clear winner as Arab minority parties hold potential balance of power
articles.title: Israeli Arab parties hold key as Netanyahu falls short of majority
articles.summary: Results from the October 27, 2026 election showed Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's right-wing bloc leading with 54 seats against opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot's 49 seats, both falling short of the 61-seat majority. Arab minority lists projected to win 17 seats could influence government formation, while both leaders signaled potential military actions regarding Iran alongside United States President Donald Trump.
articles.description: With more than three-quarters of the vote counted, Benjamin Netanyahu's right-wing bloc was slightly ahead but still short of a majority

articles.headline: Tens of thousands flee Ethiopia fighting into neighbouring Kenya
articles.title: Tens of thousands flee Ethiopia fighting into neighbouring Kenya
articles.description: Tens of thousands of people have crossed into Kenya, fleeing fighting between regional forces in Ethiopia’s Moyale town.

articles.headline: Record turnout marks inconclusive Israeli election as parties weigh coalition and Arab alliances
articles.title: Israel’s election: The battle between change and anti-Palestinian sentiment
articles.summary: Voter turnout reached 77.7 percent in Tuesday's election, the highest since 1999, as outgoing Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's coalition secured 54 seats and Gadi Eisenkot's opposition won 49 seats. With neither bloc reaching the 61-seat majority, President Isaac Herzog will consult party leaders to determine who receives the mandate to form a government within 28 days.
articles.description: With both blocs short of a majority, parties face a choice: to break the taboo on Arab allies or return to the polls.

articles.headline: Israeli leaders claim mandates following inconclusive general election
articles.title: Netanyahu and rival each claim mandate after tight Israel election
articles.summary: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and opposition challenger Gadi Eisenkot both vowed to form a government on October 28, 2026, following a general election featuring a turnout of nearly 78 percent. Exit polls showed both major blocs securing approximately 51 seats, falling short of the 61-seat majority required in parliament and raising the possibility of protracted coalition talks.
articles.description: Exit polls showed Mr. Eisenkot, a former military chief and political novice, and his opposition bloc neck and neck with Mr. Netanyahu’s hard-right camp and both well away from the threshold for a majority in Parliament

articles.headline: Supreme Court directs the Election Commission to simplify Delhi enrolment
articles.title: Delhi SIR: Supreme Court asks ECI to extend deadlines, simplify enrolment
articles.summary: The Supreme Court of India instructed the Election Commission of India on Wednesday to extend deadlines for the special intensive revision of electoral rolls in Delhi and simplify voter enrolment. The bench emphasized that Form 6 remains unchanged and granted two weeks for adjustments, noting there is currently no election taking place in the national capital.
articles.description: While addressing the ECI in the Delhi SIR case, the top court clarified that it did not judicially review the ‘logical discrepancy’ in the Bihar SIR case

articles.headline: Hackers target US Federal Election Commission website ahead of midterms
articles.title: Hackers target US campaign finance system days before midterm elections
articles.summary: Unidentified hackers targeted the United States Federal Election Commission website, forcing a temporary suspension of web-facing services days before the midterm elections. The outage disrupted the filing of critical 24 and 48-hour spending reports that track political financing. Democratic Commissioner Dara Lindenbaum confirmed systems are being restored, while officials emphasized that voter files and registration databases managed by individual states remain completely unaffected.
articles.description: An FEC email said a 'bad actor' tried to breach its systems as the US prepares for its most expensive elections ever.

articles.headline: South Korea fines Google and Apple over app market practices
articles.title: South Korea fines Google and Apple over ‘unfair’ app market practices
articles.summary: South Korea fined Alphabet unit Google and Apple a combined 63.7 billion won on Wednesday for abusing app store dominance. The Korea Media and Communications Commission penalized Google 42.9 billion won and Apple 20.8 billion won for forcing developers onto proprietary payment systems and delaying app reviews. Regulators ordered both technology giants to permit external payment links and improve review procedures for local developers.
articles.description: The Commission fined Google 42.9 billion won ($32 million) and Apple 20.8 billion won ($15.5 million) and ordered both companies to let South Korean developers use external payment links within their apps and to improve their app review procedures

articles.headline: Cyclone leaves trail of destruction in India as thousands evacuated
articles.title: Cyclone leaves trail of destruction in India as thousands evacuated
articles.description: Cyclone Arnab has left a trail of destruction along India’s eastern coast.

articles.headline: Palestinian citizens of Israel turn out in high numbers for elections
articles.title: High voter turnout among Palestinian citizens of Israel threatens Netanyahu
articles.summary: Palestinian citizens of Israel participated in parliamentary elections in unprecedented numbers, with certain towns reporting turnout rates exceeding 70 percent. The surge threatens to deny Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his right-wing coalition the 61-seat majority required to govern. Arab parties like the Joint List and the United Arab List could secure up to 17 combined seats, driven by voter opposition to current government policies and recent far-right campaigns.
articles.description: A historic turnout among Palestinian citizens of Israel positions Arab parties as kingmakers against the far right.

articles.headline: UK Chancellor John Healey unveils the government budget amid rising inflation
articles.title: Burnham’s government unveils its first UK budget: What to expect
articles.summary: British Chancellor John Healey announced the government tax and spending plans in parliament on Wednesday, aiming to tackle high inflation, national debt exceeding 3 trillion pounds, and defense funding gaps. The budget introduces potential taxes on banks and online marketplaces to fund public services and regional mayoralties, while addressing economic challenges driven by the ongoing conflict in the Middle East.
articles.description: UK chancellor to present an autumn budget amid rising living costs and energy bills.

articles.headline: Israeli military forces continue incursions across the occupied West Bank
articles.title: Israeli forces continue West Bank raids as Hebron lockdown enters sixth day
articles.summary: The Israeli army pursued ongoing military raids in Hebron during its sixth day of lockdown, searching homes and restricting residents in the occupied West Bank. Troops also detained four individuals in Tulkarem, deployed tear gas in Beita, and raided properties in Burin, following a United Nations Relief and Works Agency warning regarding the displacement of nearly 5,000 Palestinians.
articles.description: UN agency expresses 'grave concern' in Hebron and warns of echoes of 2025 'Iron Wall' operation.

articles.headline: Scientists use epigenetic control to silence hepatitis B viral DNA
articles.title: Gene therapy offers to beat hepatitis B virus by muting its DNA
articles.summary: Researchers have developed an experimental therapy called CRMA-1001 that successfully silences hepatitis B virus DNA in mice by selectively adding methylation marks without altering host genes. According to a study published on September 21 in Nature Biomedical Engineering, the technique utilizes CRISPR-Cas9 to deliver the silencing machinery, offering a promising path toward a lasting functional cure by preventing viral rebound.
articles.description: An experimental therapy called CRMA-1001 is a remarkable development because, instead of targeting the virus directly, it silences the viral DNA; this is promising because current treatments rarely eliminate the DNA, which allows the virus to rebound

articles.headline: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and rival Gadi Eisenkot face parliamentary deadlock
articles.title: Netanyahu and Eisenkot face difficult paths to power as neither set to win majority
articles.summary: Early results from Israel's election on October 28, 2026, indicate Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's Likud party emerged as the largest faction, though his right-wing bloc falls just short of a majority. Former army chief Gadi Eisenkot also claims strong public support for change. Final outcomes remain uncertain pending the counting of absentee ballots, leaving both leaders facing complex coalition negotiations.
articles.description: The two main blocs appear to have too few seats to form the next government without reliance on Arab parties.

articles.headline: Democrats lead national polls as political figures campaign ahead of midterms
articles.title: US midterms: Six days left – who leads in the polls as Trump, Obama rally
articles.summary: Democrats hold a nine-point advantage over Republicans in national polling with six days remaining before the November 3 midterm elections in the United States. President Donald Trump campaigned in Texas and prepared for an Ohio rally, while former President Barack Obama and former Vice President Kamala Harris campaigned in Georgia amid competitive Senate contests across multiple states.
articles.description: Democrats lead national polls as Trump and Obama campaign in key states six days before the US midterm elections.

articles.headline: Nordic leaders hold rare phone conversation with Russian President Vladimir Putin
articles.title: Norway and Finland hold rare phone call with Putin: What that means
articles.summary: Finnish President Alexander Stubb and Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Stoere spoke with Russian President Vladimir Putin for ninety minutes on Tuesday to discuss ending the war in Ukraine. The rare diplomatic contact preceded United States-brokered talks in Abu Dhabi next month, although Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov stated the discussion offered nothing new.
articles.description: The two Nordic leaders are attempting to influence US-brokered talks in Abu Dhabi to end the war in Ukraine.

articles.headline: Yemeni families struggle in Taiz amid severe road closures and soaring prices
articles.title: Mapping the siege of Yemen’s Taiz, and the price families are paying
articles.summary: Residents in the besieged Yemeni city of Taiz face extreme shortages of food, water, and fuel following road closures in October 2026. The United Nations warned that restricted access and security issues are blocking vital supplies. Local father Yousef Farhan noted that his income stopped due to the siege, forcing his family to cook over firewood as prices for basic goods surge.
articles.description: Three weeks into the siege of Yemen’s third-largest city, prices have doubled, and families are down to the basics.

articles.headline: Rahul Gandhi criticizes business community silence amid leadership dispute at Tata Sons
articles.title: Rahul Gandhi says Tata Group ‘being criminally destroyed’, questions India Inc.’s ‘silence’
articles.summary: Indian opposition leader Rahul Gandhi accused the country's business class of silence while alleging the Tata Group is being criminally destroyed. The comments address a boardroom dispute regarding the potential stock exchange listing of Tata Sons, opposed by Tata Trusts chairman Noel Tata. The Tata Trusts hold approximately sixty-six percent shares in the holding company.
articles.description: The Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha also said “Indian business is not Modi and Shah’s plaything”

articles.headline: Ten people killed after two trains collide in central Spain near Urda
articles.title: Train collision in Spain kills at least 30 people
articles.summary: A collision between two trains in central Spain resulted in at least ten fatalities and the derailment of two carriages on October 28, 2026. Regional government spokeswoman Esther Padilla stated that a Renfe AVE high-speed train struck the rear of a stationary Iryo train near Urda in Toledo province. Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez expressed shock as emergency medical teams and firefighters deployed to the site.
articles.description: Crash occurred near Urda in Toledo province, south of Madrid, on high-speed line connecting the capital with Seville.

articles.headline: Why the US midterms matter even if you don’t live in America
articles.title: Why the US midterms matter even if you don’t live in America
articles.description: From military aid and sanctions to trade and tariffs, the US midterms could shape decisions that affect millions.

articles.headline: Israelis vote in record numbers in general election
articles.title: Record turnout as Israeli voters deliver verdict on Netanyahu
articles.summary: Eligible citizens flocked to polling stations on October 27, 2026, creating the highest mid-day voter turnout since 1973 as the Central Elections Committee recorded 44.9 percent participation by early afternoon. The tense general election evaluated veteran Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu against centrist challenger Gadi Eisenkot amid regional conflicts, security concerns, and reports of isolated voting irregularities and arrests.
articles.description: Israelis are casting their ballots in the shadow of October 7 and the multi-front regional wars that it sparked, with the trauma from the attack still fresh and questions over accountability and security central to the campaign

articles.headline: Cyclone Arnab makes landfall in Andhra Pradesh
articles.title: At least 3 dead after Cylone Arnad hits southern India
articles.summary: Cyclone Arnab struck India's east coast on Wednesday morning with wind speeds reaching up to 135 kilometers per hour. Authorities evacuated at least 180,000 residents from Andhra Pradesh and Odisha, disrupting transport and shutting schools. While no casualties were reported, neighboring Nepal and Sri Lanka issued severe weather warnings for floods, landslides, and avalanches.
articles.description: Authorities evacuate 180,000 people as storm causes flooding, disrupting flights and train schedules.

articles.headline: Oil prices climb over one percent following refinery attack in Saudi Arabia
articles.title: Oil rises over 1% after Saudi Arabian refinery attack reignites supply risk
articles.summary: Global crude benchmarks increased by more than one percent on October 28, 2026, driven by renewed supply concerns after Yemen’s Houthis targeted a major Saudi Arabian facility with a missile. Brent crude futures rose to $115.47 a barrel. According to market sources, United States crude inventories also declined by 2.03 million barrels, while investors awaited official inventory data and an upcoming OPEC+ meeting.
articles.description: Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthis said ‌they had hit Saudi Arabia’s biggest oil refinery with a missile, intensifying their strikes against ‌the world’s second-largest crude producer

articles.headline: UN nuclear chief reports no repairs at damaged Iranian nuclear sites
articles.title: Iran hasn't tried to repair nuclear facilities damaged in Israeli-U.S. strikes: IAEA chief
articles.summary: International Atomic Energy Agency chief Rafael Grossi stated on October 27, 2026, that there is no evidence Iran has attempted to repair nuclear facilities damaged by United States and Israeli strikes. Speaking at a United Nations Security Council meeting called by Western nations, Grossi urged Tehran to grant inspectors access. Meanwhile, Iranian officials condemned the military actions and criticized Western focus on Iran's nuclear program.
articles.description: During a UN Security Council meeting, Rafael Grossi urged Iran to give inspectors access to all nuclear sites, including those damaged in the military attacks; Iran maintains that its nuclear program is peaceful

articles.headline: Elderly women and children survive Russian attack on Kharkiv
articles.title: Elderly women and children survive Russian attack on Kharkiv
articles.description: A Russian drone attack in Ukraine's Kharkiv late Tuesday forced elderly women and children to evacuate their homes.

articles.headline: United States President Donald Trump rolls back oil and gas methane rules
articles.title: Trump drastically loosens oil and gas methane rules
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump announced the termination of regulations restricting methane emissions from oil and gas producers on October 27, 2026. Speaking at a rally in Lubbock, Texas, Trump stated the move will save $45 billion and boost fossil-fuel production. Environmental groups criticized the decision, warning it removes critical oversight from the world's leading methane-emitting sector.
articles.description: Mr. Trump is pushing ways of bringing down energy costs ahead of the midterms, amid voter anger over soaring oil costs caused by his war on Iran

articles.headline: Jio Platforms makes strong market debut with shares listing at premium
articles.title: Jio Platforms debuts on stock exchanges at premium of ₹1,358 per share
articles.summary: Jio Platforms Limited completed India's largest initial public offering on October 28, 2026, listing on the National Stock Exchange and Bombay Stock Exchange at ₹1,358 per share. The ₹30,200 crore offering achieved a 21.36% premium over its issue price. The milestone elevates Jio to India's second-largest company by market capitalisation, reaching ₹12.5 lakh crore amid strong investor demand and positive broker outlooks.
articles.description: Jio becomes India’s second-largest company in terms of market capitalisation at ₹12.5 lakh crore, replacing Bharti Airtel

articles.headline: Federal Reserve expected to keep interest rates steady amid rising inflation
articles.title: Federal Reserve likely to skip rate hike despite elevated inflation
articles.summary: The United States Federal Reserve led by Chairman Kevin Warsh is anticipated to maintain interest rates on Wednesday October 28 2026 despite accelerated inflation driven by higher oil and gas prices from the Iran war. Consumer prices rose 3.7% in September. Economists warn above target inflation could persist for months affecting mortgage rates and the broader economy.
articles.description: The Fed, led by Chairman Kevin Warsh, wants to return inflation to its 2% target, which it typically does by raising its short-term interest rate. Higher borrowing costs, over time, can cool spending and slow inflation

articles.headline: Watch: What happens now after close vote in Israeli election?
articles.title: Watch: What happens now after close vote in Israeli election?
articles.description: Polls have closed in the Israeli election, but there is no clear winner.

articles.headline: Israeli exit polls project narrow edge for opposition bloc in election
articles.title: First Israeli election exit polls show narrow edge for Opposition
articles.summary: Initial exit polls following Tuesday October 27 2026 elections in Israel project the opposition bloc winning 52 or 53 seats just short of a majority in the 120 seat Knesset. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu led Likud party remains the largest single party with 24 or 25 seats. Turnout was high with major gains for Arab majority parties Raam and the Joint List.
articles.description: Israel’s current Opposition chief Yair Lapid said Benjamin Netanyahu’s bloc had suffered a “crushing defeat”, while left-wing leader Yair Golan said the public had “fired the Netanyahu government”

articles.headline: More than 100 killed in Sudanese military drone strike on Nyala market
articles.title: More than 100 people killed in Sudanese army drone attack on market, says Sudanese rights group
articles.summary: Rights group Emergency Lawyers stated that a Sudanese military drone strike on a crowded market in Nyala killed over 100 people and injured 113 others on Monday October 26 2026. The conflict which began in April 2023 involves fighting between the Sudanese army and the Rapid Support Forces creating a severe humanitarian crisis affecting millions of citizens nationwide.
articles.description: At least 113 people injured in the attack; many of those killed and injured are women and children, a rights group says

articles.headline: Mathematician dispute highlights growing concerns over artificial intelligence in science
articles.title: A bust-up between mathematicians is fuelling fears that AI could undermine science
articles.summary: A disagreement involving mathematician Tristan Buckmaster regarding an artificial intelligence solution to the Navier Stokes equations has raised questions about research integrity. While firms like Google DeepMind utilize models such as AlphaFold to accelerate scientific discoveries critics warn that generative artificial intelligence could undermine trust by introducing hallucinations and distorting findings across research fields.
articles.description: AI has made some awesome scientific discoveries. But now, questions are being raised about its accuracy

articles.headline: Indian border police chief remarks spark political controversy over Chinese troops
articles.title: India and China were easing tensions - then a border official spoke out
articles.summary: Shatrujeet Singh Kapur director general of the Indo Tibetan Border Police stated that Chinese troops returned to disputed areas in Arunachal Pradesh pitching tents deep inside Indian claimed territory. The rare public remarks triggered political fallout in Delhi with opposition leaders criticizing Prime Minister Narendra Modi while foreign ministries from both nations addressed ongoing border management.
articles.description: India-China ties were on a cautious recovery path until a border official’s remarks raised fresh doubts about ground realities.

articles.headline: China supports more elderly people than children for first time
articles.title: China's families are now supporting more old people than kids
articles.summary: Official data released by the government reveals that the ratio of dependent elderly individuals in China reached twenty-three percent last year, exceeding the figure for children. This demographic shift highlights an ageing population that could strain healthcare and pension systems, driven by rapid urbanisation and the legacy of the former one-child policy.
articles.description: The latest figures mark a major milestone as Beijing grapples with an ageing population.

articles.headline: Ukraine ceasefire expands across Kherson region for humanitarian relief
articles.title: Ceasefire extended across Ukraine's Kherson region, officials say
articles.summary: A truce initially established to deliver aid to Oleshky has been broadened throughout the wider Kherson region. Negotiated with international mediation, the agreement aims to facilitate mine-clearing operations and subsequent evacuations. Officials report that the cessation of hostilities is currently holding across the area without major incidents.
articles.description: The truce was originally planned for the stranded residents of Oleshky, and Russia and Ukraine say no breaches have been reported.

articles.headline: Studies show US voter fraud is extremely rare despite claims
articles.title: Trump says US voter fraud is 'rampant' - evidence suggests it is extremely rare
articles.summary: President Donald Trump has offered a one million dollar reward for reporting voter fraud convictions while alleging widespread cheating in postal voting and non-citizen participation. However, multiple studies and think tank databases indicate that actual instances of electoral fraud in the United States remain exceptionally uncommon.
articles.description: As the US president casts doubt on the security of the midterm elections, BBC Verify examines his claims.

articles.headline: What we know about Ukraine-Russia truce in Oleshky, brokered by Melania Trump
articles.title: What we know about Ukraine-Russia truce in Oleshky, brokered by Melania Trump
articles.description: The Russian-occupied city of Oleshky has had no electricity, gas or water for three years, as residents reported having to eat weeds to survive.

articles.headline: Potential Democratic midterm victory could create complex diplomatic challenges for Europe
articles.title: Why a Democratic win in US midterms could adversely affect Europe
articles.summary: Analysts suggest a Democratic victory in the United States midterm elections could foster complacency regarding European far-right movements and pressure Ukraine into unfavourable peace deals with Russia. Polling indicates declining trust in the United States, with only 31 percent of Europeans viewing Washington as their most trustworthy ally, down from 51 percent in 2024 under President Joe Biden.
articles.description: Complacency about rising far-right movements and renewed pressure on Ukraine could be the result.

articles.headline: Liverpool and Manchester City advance in League Cup following penalty shootouts
articles.title: Carabao Cup: Liverpool beats Chelsea on penalties, Man City survives Brighton scare
articles.summary: Liverpool defeated Chelsea in a penalty shootout to reach the League Cup quarterfinals following a 1-1 draw at Anfield on Wednesday. Holders Manchester City also advanced after drawing 2-2 with Brighton and winning on penalties at the Etihad Stadium. In other matches, Bournemouth defeated Aston Villa 3-0, and Crystal Palace secured a 1-0 victory against Fulham.
articles.description: Liverpool to face Bournemouth in quarterfinals; Man City plays Bradford City

articles.headline: Turkiye offers maritime boundary agreement to Egypt amid improving bilateral ties
articles.title: Can Turkiye’s Libya breakthrough reshape Eastern Mediterranean diplomacy?
articles.summary: Turkiye renewed an offer to sign a maritime boundary agreement with Egypt on Wednesday, according to the Turkish Ministry of National Defence. The proposal follows a decision by Libya's eastern-based parliament in Tobruk to approve a 2019 maritime accord with Ankara. While the diplomatic outreach complicates Egypt's position and tests regional alignments, Turkish and Egyptian officials continue working to strengthen bilateral cooperation.
articles.description: Ankara wins backing from former adversaries in Libya for maritime border agreement, but other diplomatic tests remain.

articles.headline: Directorate of Vigilance and Anti-Corruption searches former minister K.N. Nehru's residence
articles.title: DVAC searches ex-Minister K.N. Nehru’s residence in Tiruchi
articles.summary: Anti-corruption officials in Tamil Nadu searched the Tiruchi residence of former minister K.N. Nehru on Thursday as part of an investigation into an alleged cash-for-jobs scam. The Directorate of Vigilance and Anti-Corruption launched operations across 25 locations following a Madras High Court clearance. DMK chief M.K. Stalin condemned the raids as politically motivated vendetta tactics ahead of upcoming by-elections.
articles.description: The operation, carried out by a team headed by a Deputy Superintendent of Police, began at around 7 a.m.

articles.headline: Researchers in Keralam study potential links between gut bacteria and Parkinson's disease
articles.title: Study in Keralam sheds light on link between gut bacteria, Parkinson’s disease
articles.summary: Scientists at Cochin University of Science and Technology and the Sree Chitra Tirunal Institute for Medical Sciences and Technology published findings revealing distinct gut bacteria differences in Parkinson's disease patients. Funded by the Indian Council of Medical Research, the study analyzed stool samples from 65 patients and 65 healthy individuals using metagenomic sequencing to explore early diagnostic tests and treatments.
articles.description: Researchers from CUSAT and SCTIMST, Thiruvananthapuram, find significant differences between gut bacteria of Parkinson’s patients and those of healthy individuals

articles.headline: Thane Police warn protesters against highway blockades during murder investigation demonstrations
articles.title: Thane Police warn of action over highway blockades amid Purnekar murder protests, say SIT probe on track
articles.summary: Thane Police announced warnings on Wednesday regarding illegal road blockades following violent protests over the murder of Pradeep Purnekar. Joint Commissioner Panjabrao Ugle stated that a 23-member Special Investigation Team has arrested five suspects and gathered forensic evidence while handling family allegations of political interference. Authorities urged residents to refrain from demonstrations that severely disrupt public movement.
articles.description: The protests, which continued overnight, followed allegations by Purnekar’s family that police had failed to act against former Thane mayor Meenakshi Shinde and her husband Rajendra Shinde despite evidence allegedly linking them to the murder conspiracy

articles.headline: Wageningen University researchers test salt marsh resilience against large artificial waves
articles.title: How the humble salt marsh softens the ocean’s fury
articles.summary: Researchers at Wageningen University and Research transported live salt marsh samples from the Dutch Wadden Sea to a large flume facility at the Deltares Research Institute. Testing revealed that dense root networks successfully held sediments together under severe wave action despite substantial surface flora damage. The study highlights the ecological value of coastal salt marshes as natural protective buffers against storms.
articles.description: The Hindu’s weekly Science for All newsletter explains all things Science, without the jargon

articles.headline: Congress defeats BJP in Nagpur as opposition alliance leads Maharashtra polls
articles.title: Maharashtra MLC election: Congress trumps BJP in Nagpur, MVA leads 3-2 in State
articles.summary: The Indian National Congress defeated the Bharatiya Janata Party in Nagpur during the Maharashtra Legislative Council elections. Overall, the opposition Maha Vikas Aghadi alliance secured three of the five contested graduates and teachers constituencies, while the ruling Mahayuti alliance won two seats. Opposition leaders criticized Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis over the results and highlighted that the election was conducted using ballot papers.
articles.description: While the NCP SP called for going back to ballot papers for holding elections, the BJP called for introspection among the alliance partners

articles.headline: Telangana electoral rolls face high rejection and deletion rates during revision
articles.title: Telangana SIR: Form-6 rejections and Form-7 deletions unusually high during pre-SIR period
articles.summary: According to the office of the Chief Electoral Officer, Telangana recorded unusually high rejection and deletion rates during the Special Intensive Revision of Electoral Rolls. Out of total applications processed across 119 constituencies, authorities rejected close to 27 percent of Form-6 applications, while millions of voter names were deleted using Form-7, creating significant exclusions in the final voter rolls.
articles.description: The number of rejections constitutes close to 27% of the total Form-6 applications processed during Pre-SIR and SIR phases, which is very high

articles.headline: Incredible celebrations as last patient leaves a DRC Ebola centre
articles.title: Incredible celebrations as last patient leaves a DRC Ebola centre
articles.description: Footage shows healthcare workers celebrating at an Ebola treatment centre in DR Congo after the last patient left.

articles.headline: Minnesota fraud scheme participant Salim Said receives thirty-year prison sentence
articles.title: 30-year sentence in Minnesota fraud that drew Trump backlash
articles.summary: Salim Said, a thirty-seven-year-old restaurant operator in Minneapolis, Minnesota, received a thirty-year prison sentence for his involvement in a forty-four million dollar COVID-nineteen pandemic food programme fraud scheme. US District Judge Nancy Brasel delivered the sentence on Wednesday following a case that drew national scrutiny and intense political pressure from President Donald Trump.
articles.description: Government says Salim Said hit the jackpot in a scheme claiming to feed needy children during the COVID-19 pandemic.

articles.headline: NIMHANS neurology casualty reports high stroke patient volume in Karnataka
articles.title: 40% of patients at NIMHANS neurology casualty have stroke; KMCRI in Hubbali treats 120 cases a month
articles.summary: Nearly 40 percent of patients seeking neurological care at the NIMHANS casualty in Bengaluru are stroke victims, with 705 cases reported monthly. To address this urgent demand, a hub-and-spoke collaborative model linking NIMHANS with the Karnataka Institute of Medical Sciences and Research Institute in Hubballi helps doctors manage approximately 120 monthly stroke cases in northern districts using teleconsultation.
articles.description: Hub-and-spoke model extends specialised stroke care to northern Karnataka, reducing the need for emergency transfers to Bengaluru. World Stroke Day is observed on October 29.

articles.headline: Al Jazeera speaks to El-Sayed as religion becomes flashpoint in Senate race
articles.title: Al Jazeera speaks to El-Sayed as religion becomes flashpoint in Senate race
articles.description: Democratic candidate Abdul El-Sayed is pushing back against attacks over his Muslim faith.

articles.headline: Utah files criminal charges against prediction market Kalshi and cofounders
articles.title: Kalshi, cofounders hit with criminal charges in US state of Utah
articles.summary: Utah Attorney General Derek Brown filed criminal charges against prediction market Kalshi, CEO Tarek Mansour, and COO Luana Lopes Lara on Wednesday. The Salt Lake City court complaint accuses the platform of twelve counts of online gambling promotion and facilitating undercover sports wagers, escalating a jurisdictional showdown between state authorities and the Trump administration.
articles.description: The charges come after a federal judge ruled that Utah could enforce its anti-gambling laws against prediction markets.

articles.headline: Bolsonaro in Miami: I am the ‘true president-elect’
articles.title: Bolsonaro in Miami: I am the ‘true president-elect’
articles.description: Flavio Bolsonaro claimed to be the ‘true president-elect’ of Brazil in his first statement since fleeing to the US.

articles.headline: RSS well-wishers register RSS Friends as a foreign agent in the United States
articles.title: ‘RSS Friends’ registers in U.S. to step up outreach, correct inaccuracies
articles.summary: A group named RSS Friends has officially registered with the United States Department of Justice as a foreign agent under the Foreign Agents Registration Act. The organization lists the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh in New Delhi as its principal and aims to enhance public outreach, engage with community leaders, and correct inaccurate information regarding the India-based volunteer group.
articles.description: The RSS Friends, which provided a Georgia address in the registration document, listed Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh, Keshavkunj, New Delhi as its “foreign principal”

articles.headline: Karnataka electoral rolls potentially miss over six million voters
articles.title: Karnataka SIR: 64.5 lakh voters potentially missing in rolls, majority of them young
articles.summary: Approximately sixty-four point five million electors are potentially missing from Karnataka's final electoral rolls following a Special Intensive Revision exercise released on October 27, 2026. Calculations based on the Chief Electoral Officer's data indicate that young adults aged eighteen to twenty-nine account for the majority of excluded voters. Economist Jean Dreze noted that the resulting elector-to-population ratio falls significantly below projected adult demographic estimates for the state.
articles.description: Elector-to-population ratio released officially by Karnataka CEO shows under-enrolment of about 64.5 lakh electors, of whom roughly 38.41 lakh are in the 18 to 29 age group.

articles.headline: Congress candidate Abhijeet Wanjari retains Nagpur division graduates constituency seat
articles.title: In setback to BJP, Congress wins Nagpur MLC seat
articles.summary: Congress candidate Abhijeet Wanjari defeated Bharatiya Janata Party rival Sudhakar Kohale by 3,271 votes in the Nagpur Division Graduates constituency election. The victory delivers a significant political blow to the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party in the hometown of Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis and Union Minister Nitin Gadkari, following a counting process that concluded on October 29, 2026.
articles.description: The Congress fielded sitting MLC Abhijeet Wanjari, who secured 67,231 votes, while the BJP fielded former MLA Sudhakar Kohale, who secured 63,960 votes

articles.headline: Digital Personal Data Protection Act does not infringe on press freedom, says Ashwini Vaishnaw
articles.title: Digital Personal Data Protection Act does not infringe on press freedom: Ashwini Vaishnaw
articles.summary: Information Technology Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw stated on October 28, 2026, that the Digital Personal Data Protection Act protects personal data without undermining journalistic independence guaranteed by the Constitution. Addressing media concerns over investigative reporting, he invited editors for dialogue and noted that the government is open to parliamentary amendments to explicitly safeguard media activities if necessary.
articles.description: IT Minister invites editors and media professionals to engage in open dialogue with government to discuss concerns surrounding the law

articles.headline: Enforcement Directorate attaches Mohammad Ali Jauhar University land and buildings
articles.title: ED attaches land, buildings of Mohammad Ali Jauhar University in Rampur in money laundering case
articles.summary: The Enforcement Directorate provisionally attached land and buildings belonging to Mohammad Ali Jauhar University in Rampur, valued at 426.46 crore rupees with a market value of approximately 1,170 crore rupees. According to an official statement on October 28, 2026, the action falls under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act regarding a case against the Maulana Mohammad Ali Jauhar Trust and former Uttar Pradesh cabinet minister Mohammad Azam Khan.
articles.description: “ED found that funds meant for public works were diverted to the University, government works were executed on its private campus, and funds from contractors who had been allotted government contracts were routed back to the Trust as donations,” the statement said

articles.headline: Indian defense scientists urge end-to-end domestic semiconductor manufacturing
articles.title: India must make its defence chips end-to-end, say scientists
articles.summary: Senior researchers speaking at a semiconductor summit warned that India's network-centric weapons remain vulnerable due to heavy reliance on imported microchips. Experts stressed the urgent necessity to develop complete domestic capabilities spanning design, materials, and fabrication to secure future military hardware against potential foreign compromise.
articles.description: At The Hindu Semiconductor Summit, V.K. Saraswat, A. Sivathanu Pillai and Deleep Nair warn that imported chips leave network-centric weapons vulnerable, and that waiting until 2030-35 for advanced nodes would be too late

articles.headline: Industry leaders say chip war exposes India semiconductor vulnerabilities
articles.title: Chip war exposes India’s semiconductor vulnerabilities, industry leaders say
articles.summary: Industry leaders meeting at the Semiconductor Summit 2026 in Chennai warned that geopolitical tensions expose India's technological and supply-chain vulnerabilities. Sharat Kaul of iNEMI urged progressive ecosystem development, while Indichip Semiconductors CEO Sandrep Garg noted domestic manufacturing gaps for essential gases and chemicals, urging the government to grant the sector industry status.
articles.description: U.S.–China tensions underscore need for domestic technology capabilities and resilient supply chains; industry flags gaps in materials, manufacturing expertise and specialised talent

articles.headline: Israelis rally for Jewish-Arab government after election gains
articles.title: Israelis rally for Jewish-Arab government after election gains
articles.description: Israelis rallied for a Jewish-Arab gov’t after parties representing Israel’s Arab citizens made gains in the election.

articles.headline: Romanian court extends pre-trial detention of far-right politician Calin Georgescu
